question_text: There are 4 copies alike each of 3 different books. Find the number of ways of arranging these 12 books on a shelf in a single row.

recall_prompt: Say how you would count the arrangements of twelve books, four alike copies of each of three titles, in a row — what you count first and which formula you use.
insider_note: The divisor is one 4! per title, three times in all: 12!/(4!·4!·4!) = 34,650. Writing 4! once counts the copies of two titles as if they were different books.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Count the letters and the repeats
steps.margin_note: First mark. 3 × 4 = 12 books; the 4 copies of each title are alike, so three groups of 4.
lines: Four alike of the first book, four alike of
the second, four alike of the third.

recall.must_convey: That there are 12 books in three groups of 4 alike copies.
accept: twelve books, three groups of four alike
three times four is twelve books with four copies of each alike
the repeats are four, four and four
twelve books, prathi book ki four alike copies
count the total and the alike groups first

steps.why: Alike letters cannot be told apart, so swapping them does not give a new arrangement. The count of each repeated letter is what the formula divides by, so it must be found before anything else.
common_mistakes: Answering 12! as if every copy were different.
Answering 3! by arranging only the titles.

steps.label: Apply n!/(p!·q!·r!)

recall.must_convey: That the count is 12 factorial over 4 factorial cubed.
accept: twelve factorial over four factorial four factorial four factorial
twelve factorial by four factorial cubed
divide twelve factorial by twenty four three times
twelve factorial by four factorial into four factorial into four factorial
the answer is twelve factorial over four factorial cubed which is thirty four thousand six hundred fifty

steps.why: n! counts the arrangements as if every letter were different; each group of p alike letters has been counted p! times over, so dividing by p! for each group leaves the true count.
common_mistakes: Dividing by 4! once instead of three times.
Dividing by 12! ÷ 3 or some other guess — the denominator is the product of the group factorials.
